title: U.S. House · Colorado's 1st District

context.text: This is an open seat: Melat Kiros defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette and Wanda James 53.2%-39.8%-7.0% in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, so DeGette will not appear on the November ballot. Christy Peterson advanced unopposed from the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Melat Kiros
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette

summary.text: Melat Kiros is a Denver attorney who defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette in the Democratic primary for Colorado's 1st Congressional District. She immigrated to the U.S. from Tigray, Ethiopia in 1998.

background.text: Immigrated to Denver, Colorado, from Tigray, Ethiopia, in 1998 with her family.
Earned bachelor's degrees in Political Science and Economics from Washington College (2018) and a law degree from the University of Notre Dame (2022).
Career experience includes working as a lawyer and, earlier, as a barista.

priorities.text: Campaign finance and lobbying reform, plus congressional term limits, to reduce the influence of money in politics.
Expanding voting rights and consolidating elections into a single day with a shorter election cycle.
Codifying access to housing, health care, nutritious food and public education as basic needs for every American.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will always stand for Medicare for All and describes health care access as directly linked to life expectancy and economic outcomes.
Says she will always stand for universal childcare as part of putting working families first.
Campaign website calls for an arms embargo and says tax dollars should not support what she describes as a genocide, opposing continued unconditional military aid.

summary.text: Christy Peterson is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 1st Congressional District. She works in accounting and describes her candidacy as focused on public safety and reducing government spending in Denver.

background.text: Graduated from Chatfield Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from San Diego State University in 2006.
Career experience includes working in accounting/office management in construction; states she is pursuing a doctorate in natural and functional medicine.

priorities.text: Public safety: says reducing crime and 'soft on crime' policies in Denver is her top priority, arguing this would let businesses and visitors return to the city.
Reducing government waste, fraud and abuse, and creating incentives for business growth and job creation.

positions.summary: Says making cities safe again is her top priority and that crime and lax enforcement have driven residents and businesses away.
States support for protecting the right to bear arms in her Ballotpedia survey response.

candidates.name: Chad Humphrey

summary.text: Chad Humphrey is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 1st Congressional District, a retired Marine Corps officer and tech entrepreneur.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 1993 to 2013, including a combat tour.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Occidental College and an MBA from Pepperdine University.
Currently works as a technology entrepreneur.

priorities.text: Lists his three key campaign messages as restoring the Constitution, ending the Federal Reserve and the IRS, and stopping what he calls endless wars.
Says he is personally passionate about free markets.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, which did not directly address any of the 15 tracked issue statements; no separate campaign website was found.

candidates.name: Shimon Blau

summary.text: Shimon Blau is an independent candidate for Colorado's 1st Congressional District, a Denver-born physician and small-business owner who rejects PAC contributions and says he would caucus with Democrats if elected.

background.text: Born and raised in Denver's Sloan's Lake neighborhood, the son of immigrants; his father was a Holocaust survivor from Poland who served in the U.S. Army during the Korean War before earning an engineering degree from Columbia University.
Is a board-certified physician specializing in interventional spine and pain management; returned to Denver in 2013 to complete his medical fellowship and build his practice.
Owns a small medical practice/business in the Denver area.

priorities.text: Says he is running as an independent who rejects contributions from PACs and special-interest groups, saying he answers only to the people of the district.

Says he would caucus with Democrats and support Rep. Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as a check on the Trump administration, while remaining willing to oppose Democratic-backed policies he disagrees with.
Wants to strengthen Denver's local economy by supporting small businesses, encouraging investment, and improving public safety.

positions.summary: Says he supports a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions and does not believe government should interfere in women's healthcare.
positions.quote: I support a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions, and I support the freedom of consenting adults to marry the person they love. These are deeply personal decisions, and I do not believe government should interfere in women's healthcare or in the private lives of consenting adults.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response found; background and positions are drawn from his campaign website (blauforcongress.com), which does not have a dedicated issues page but discusses his priorities on the home page.

candidates.name: Critter Milton

summary.text: Critter Milton is the Unity Party candidate for Colorado's 1st Congressional District, a perennial candidate and former financial advisor who lives in Alma, Colorado.

background.text: Earned a degree from the University of Denver in 2006 and attended the College for Financial Planning for graduate study; spent over a decade as a financial advisor.
Has been affiliated with Multiple Summits for Multiple Sclerosis as a member of its organizing committee.
Has run for federal office repeatedly since 2020, including for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District and U.S. Senate in 2020 and this seat in 2024.

priorities.text: In his most recent completed Ballotpedia survey (2022), listed his three key campaign messages simply as 'Unity, Unity, Unity.'
In an earlier (2020) survey, said his priorities included free universal education using technology, action on climate change, and ending prohibition by legalizing currently banned substances.

candidates.researchNotes: Milton has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his most recent completed survey was in 2022 (for a different U.S. House race), so priorities above are dated and not necessarily current for this 2026 campaign. No campaign website with current issue positions was found.
